correctness.rationale: For rank-one corner loss, H-cyclic subspace B=span{H^j c} equals the span of nonzero spectral projections P_E c; on B^⊥ absorption vanishes, while every eigenvalue of K|B has strictly negative imaginary part, giving decay even with Jordan blocks. Open path P_{p−1} has eigenvalues ±(ζ_p^j+ζ_p^{-j}) and nonzero sine endpoint components, so dim B equals number of distinct pairwise eigenvalue sums. For equal p, the m=(p−1)/2 real cyclotomic basis elements are Q-linearly independent by the Φ_p constant-term argument; the sums are 0, ±2t_j, and ±t_i±t_j giving 2m²+1. For distinct odd primes cyclotomic intersection is Q and common difference is integer; field traces kill nonzero integer differences at primes>=7 and the (3,5) small case has incompatible differences 2 versus 1. Thus all (p−1)(q−1) sums are distinct. Independent 70-digit numerical spectral computation for all 25 pairs p,q in {3,5,7,11,13} reproduced exact ranks (R3_VISIBLE_SPECTRUM_PRIME_GRID_OK); proof is cyclotomic, not numeric.
residual_risks: Only uniformly hopped open grids, odd-prime shifted side lengths and one corner sink; no rate bound uniform in p,q.
The intersection of distinct prime cyclotomic fields is Q, and the trace argument are essential; numeric ranks alone would not certify them.

value.rationale: Absorption in a finite quantum walk is directly controlled by detectable spectral support. The exact dichotomy changes capture from unity for different prime shifts to near 1/2 on equal-prime squares, and applies to arbitrary initial densities and every positive sink strength. This is a motivated structural arithmetic resonance effect rather than an arbitrary grid-size experiment.
residual_risks: No uniform finite-time absorption rate or disorder robustness.

limitations: All conclusions require uniform real nonzero hopping, one positive corner imaginary sink, and open paths with odd-prime shifted side sizes.
Absorption asymptotic is long-time; no finite-time optimization.
